articles.title: Designing a Confidence-Aware AI Takeoff Pipeline for Construction Drawings
articles.excerpt: Construction takeoff looks like an object-detection problem until the first real drawing set arrives. Symbols overlap. Legends change between designers. Scanned sheets have noise and skew. The scale p…
articles.body: Construction takeoff looks like an object-detection problem until the first real drawing set arrives. Symbols overlap. Legends change between designers. Scanned sheets have noise and skew. The scale printed in the title block may not match the viewport. A schedule may contain equipment that never appears clearly on plan. Then an addendum changes three sheets while leaving the rest of the bid package untouched. A production takeoff system therefore needs more than a model that returns bounding boxes. It needs a confidence-aware pipeline that preserves evidence, routes ambiguity to a reviewer, and keeps quantities traceable through revisions. This article describes an implementation pattern for building that pipeline.

articles.title: The cheapest GitHub Actions runners in 2026: what 100,000 minutes cost
articles.excerpt: I build open source developer tools, mostly supergateway and Supercov. This month I looked at what their CI actually uses. From October 1 to 27, those repos ran 534,311 minutes on GitHub Actions. GitH…
articles.body: I build open source developer tools, mostly supergateway and Supercov . This month I looked at what their CI actually uses. From October 1 to 27, those repos ran 534,311 minutes on GitHub Actions. GitHub billed us $0 , because the repos are public. At list price the same minutes come to $8,292 . macOS is 15% of the minutes and 59% of the money. Most of the rest is test matrices: Supercov runs its compatibility tests on Linux, Linux Arm, macOS, Windows and Windows Arm on every pull request, including the ones coding agents open. If those repos were private, that would be a real bill. That question is how we ended up building our own runners, SuperCI , which start a machine per job in your own cloud account.

articles.title: Laser pointer for Obsidian: how my messy tldraw canvas during midsems became a plugin
articles.excerpt: For the past few weeks I've been taking notes and reading in Obsidian for my midsems, and it worked fine until I had to explain a topic to a friend. I wanted the shared-whiteboard experience: copy the…
articles.body: For the past few weeks I've been taking notes and reading in Obsidian for my midsems, and it worked fine until I had to explain a topic to a friend. I wanted the shared-whiteboard experience: copy the question somewhere, draw around it, point at the pieces. My tool for that part was tldraw, mostly because of its laser pointer. Two problems showed up fast. The tldraw canvas just kept growing, one topic stacked under another, until finding "that thing I explained earlier" meant scrolling archaeology. And switching apps in the middle of an explanation broke the flow every time. So the obvious idea finally landed: the laser should live inside Obsidian, where the notes already are. I searched a lot for an existing plugin and found nothing, so I wrote one.
articles.author: Akash Pattnaik

articles.excerpt: In Part 1 we covered what Maestro is, how it works and how it compares to Appium, XCUITest, Detox and the paid device clouds. Now it is time to write real tests. In this article we will: Build a small…
articles.body: In Part 1 we covered what Maestro is, how it works and how it compares to Appium, XCUITest, Detox and the paid device clouds. Now it is time to write real tests. In this article we will: Build a small SwiftUI app with a login screen and a to-do list. Make it testable with accessibility identifiers. Write a Maestro suite with reusable sub-flows, environment variables, conditional logic, JavaScript and tags. Run it locally, generate reports and debug failures. Look at how the same test would look in XCUITest, and where AI agents fit in. Everything here uses the free, open-source Maestro CLI. The full app is about 120 lines of Swift, so you can copy it into a new Xcode project and follow along.

articles.title: Android is locking down permissions to keep apps from messing with your contacts
articles.excerpt: Google is putting apps that want to add to or change your contacts under new scrutiny.
articles.body: TL;DR Android apps that get permission to change your contacts can currently access all of them. Google’s interested in limiting that with a system that distinguishes between individual and bulk edits. The first components are arriving with Android 17 QPR2 later this year. Keeping Android users safe is one of the most challenging problems Google faces with its mobile operating system, and one of the many ways it’s managed to address the task is through the development of Android’s permission system . By only granting apps a narrow set of permissions that they truly need, we can limit the ability of secretly malicious or otherwise compromised apps to do harm. Today we’re leaning about an update to how permissions work when it comes to contacts, and why Google’s making the change.

articles.title: Astronomers discover the secrets of 'string of pearls' supernova relic and the zombie star at its heart
articles.excerpt: Scientists are still learning about a cosmic 'string of pearls,' a unique celestial relic left by a supernova witnessed by humanity around 850 years ago, which has a zombie star at its heart.
articles.body: Scientists are still learning about a cosmic "string of pearls," a unique celestial relic left by a supernova explosion that humanity witnessed around 850 years ago. That is thanks to the most detailed observation of the dandelion-shaped chains of gas and supernova debris that comprise Pa 30, the only supernova remnant of its type observed in the Milky Way . What makes Pa 30 even more unique is that it has a rare "zombie star" at its heart. Supernovas like the one that created Pa 30 are called Type Ia supernovas; they happen when a dead star called a white dwarf overfeeds on a companion star like a cosmic vampire. This overfeeding triggers a runaway nuclear explosion that usually destroys the white dwarf.

articles.body: PALO ALTO, Calif. — Cowboy Space just showed us how it plans to become a big player in the final frontier. The California-based company, which is run by Robinhood co-founder Baiju Bhatt, intends to operate a constellation of 20,000 AI data centers in low Earth orbit (LEO). It will build those satellites in house and launch them on a homegrown rocket — a vehicle Cowboy Space unveiled here on Monday night (Oct. 26), at an event it called "Big Sky Rising." "It's a fundamentally novel approach to rocketry in the modern era, in our opinion," Bhatt said during the event. "The idea is that you have a two-stage rocket where the upper stage of the rocket itself transforms into the satellite." Big Iron's first stage will be reusable.

articles.title: November full moon 2026: When, where and how to see the Beaver Moon
articles.excerpt: Your guide to November's full Beaver Moon, from peak times to skywatching highlights.
articles.body: The November full moon reaches maximum illumination at 9:53 a.m. EST (1453 GMT) on Nov. 24, as the lunar disk sits opposite the sun in Earth's sky, appearing fully lit by its rays. November's full moon is traditionally known as the " Beaver Moon ", because it rises around the time when the small mammals take refuge in their dens, having stored enough food to survive the long winter months, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac . The Nov. 24 full moon also happens to be the first of three consecutive " supermoons ". The non-scientific term is often bestowed on full moons that occur when the natural satellite is within 90% of perigee, when the moon is closest to Earth in its elliptical orbit.

articles.body: Anthropic cofounder and CEO Dario Amodei. | Bloomberg via Getty Images Anthropic wants to have it both ways. With its impending IPO, it wants to tap the vast riches of the public markets and insists it doesn't want to compromise its core mission of developing AI safely and for the benefit of humanity. But greater model capabilities bring greater risks, and shareholders eager for returns may have little patience for costly safety measures that slow products on their way to market. Sam Altman, the CEO of Anthropic's archrival, OpenAI, has cited investor pressures as one reason the company is not pursuing an IPO this year. articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 27, 1961: NASA launches Saturn I rocket on 1st test flight from Florida to set stage for the mighty Saturn V moon rocket
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 27, 1961, NASA launched the first test flight of its new Saturn I space launch vehicle. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 27, 1961, NASA launched the first test flight of its new Saturn I space launch vehicle. The Saturn I rocket was the United States' first heavy-lift rocket designed to launch big payloads beyond low Earth orbit. This was also the first test flight of any rocket in the Saturn family of rockets, which includes the Saturn V that was used to launch astronauts to the moon during the Apollo program . The Saturn I was enormous compared to every rocket that came before it. It was almost three times as tall as the Jupiter-C rocket, which launched the first American satellite into orbit in 1958. It also produced more than 10 times the amount of thrust that the Jupiter-C rocket could. The liquid-powered rocket launched on its maiden voyage from Cape Canaveral.

articles.title: Mars rover tracks from a historic drive | Space photo of the day for Oct. 27, 2026
articles.excerpt: Rover tracks can be seen on the Martian surface, left behind by NASA's Perseverance Mars rover.
articles.body: Rover tracks can be seen on the Martian surface, left behind by NASA's Perseverance Mars rover. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) NASA's Perseverance Mars rover left a mark on the Martian landscape when it passed a historic milestone driving across the Red Planet. What is it? On Oct. 11, Perseverance passed 28.10 miles (45.22 kilometers) driven on Mars. This is farther than anything has ever traveled on the surface of another world, earning the rover the interplanetary driving record . Previously, this record was set by NASA's Opportunity rover, and it took Opportunity roughly 14 years to drive this far. Perseverance traversed this distance in just over 5 years.

articles.body: This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. Will the real Anthropic please stand up? After weeks of frenzied speculation, Anthropic has filed its IPO prospectus. The 335-page document (100 pages or so are focused on risks) lays out the company’s unique view of the technology it is building and how it believes it will change the world. But Anthropic has been honing its storytelling skills for years. Its public messaging is a master class in narrative capture, presenting it as different things to different people: an AI safety organization, a profit-driven megacorp, and a group hell-bent on creating superhuman technology. These roles come with huge tensions.
